pathway.title: BWX Technologies, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The business is the strongest support: sole-source US naval nuclear demand gives creditors visible revenue that a competitor cannot easily take. Government Operations earned 81.43% of segment operating income in the nine months of 2026 on 66.88% of segment revenue, 88% of that revenue came from the US Government, and the issuer calls its Navy fuel plant the sole provider and competition limited. Backlog cover rose from 1.79x revenue at FY2024 to 2.38x, and the unfunded share of backlog fell from 29.63% at FY2025 to 23.03%. The exposure is one customer's annual appropriation cycle, so a continuing resolution or shutdown would delay awards and cash timing before it threatened repayment, and on termination the contracts generally allow recovery of costs and profit on work done. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2024-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation D11; calculation D12; calculation D21; calculation D22; calculation D23; calculation D24; calculation D80

Liquidity is a strength and refinancing is a 2028 to 2030 task rather than a near-term risk. Liquidity of USD 1.82 billion is cash of USD 568.53 million plus USD 1,248.60 million available under the undrawn revolver after letters of credit, and the USD 400 million of senior notes due in 2028 are covered by cash alone. Pro forma cash and net debt after the medical business sale agreed on 2026-07-31 are not established. Contractual interest on the notes is only USD 33.00 million a year, before revolver commitment fees, because 60.98% of principal is zero-coupon convertible notes due in 2030. Both senior notes can be redeemed at par at any time, which gives flexibility, but the revolver's 2030 maturity comes forward if unsecured debt due within 91 days exceeds the facility's EBITDA measure, unless net leverage is at or below 2.00x or liquidity is at least 125% of that debt, which for the convertible notes means USD 1,562.50 million; the agreement's definitions are not supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 73; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D28; calculation D29; calculation D38; calculation D39; calculation D40; calculation D75

Leverage is moderate and has eased from its peak, but it depends on how joint-venture income is treated. Gross debt over derived last-twelve-months EBITDA is 3.56x against 3.92x at FY2025, and net debt of USD 1.45 billion is 2.56x against 2.95x. Pro forma net debt and net leverage after the pending medical business sale are not established, and the EBITDA still includes the medical business and only one quarter of Precision Components Group. Equity income of joint ventures is 15.93% of that EBITDA, and without it gross leverage would be 4.23x and net leverage 3.04x, although joint-venture dividends of USD 201.54 million exceeded income of USD 181.65 million over FY2023 to FY2025, so the nine-month retention looks like timing rather than loss. The facility's maximum leverage covenant is 4.00x, rising to 4.50x for up to four quarters after a material acquisition, and compliance is reported at every date, but the covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 108; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D33; calculation D34; calculation D35; calculation D36; calculation D37; calculation D42; calculation D44; calculation D45; calculation D46; calculation D47; calculation D48; calculation D75

Margin resilience is the weakest financial dimension: EBITDA margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points, from 18.49% in FY2023 to 15.79% over the last twelve months. Three things drove it. Commercial Operations, with a nine-month operating margin of 8.29% against 18.01% for Government Operations, grew 62.10%, largely on acquisitions, while Government Operations grew 3.26%, and two acquisitions supplied 52.95% of nine-month revenue growth. Segment margins also slipped in FY2025, with Government Operations at 16.80% against 18.45% in FY2023. Selling and administrative costs rose from 11.20% to 12.33% of revenue, and unallocated corporate costs rose USD 19.73 million in the nine months of 2026. The pressure may be easing: EBITDA margin was 13.73% in the fourth quarter of 2025, 15.96% in the first half of 2026 and 17.38% in the third quarter against 16.37% a year earlier, and the Government Operations margin was 19.2% against 15.8%. But the nine-month margin of 16.46% is still below the 16.95% of a year earlier, so one quarter is not yet a trend. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 79; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 136; calculation D94; calculation D95; calculation D02; calculation D03; calculation D04; calculation D05; calculation D06; calculation D07; calculation D08; calculation D09; calculation D100; calculation D101; calculation D10; calculation D13; calculation D14; calculation D15; calculation D16; calculation D17; calculation D18; calculation D19; calculation D20; calculation D80

Free cash flow is solid and improving, but its conversion is flattered by supplier timing and the business is still investing heavily. Last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 372.32 million is 65.50% of EBITDA, up from 46.01% in FY2023, 54.62% in FY2024 and 57.49% in FY2025, and the nine-month payables inflow of USD 150.33 million was 33.28% of nine-month operating cash flow; if that inflow reversed, last-twelve-months free cash flow would be USD 221.99 million, or 39.05% of EBITDA. This narrows the reading in Financial foundation: the combined line for contracts in progress and advance billings was an outflow of USD 49.11 million in the nine months, so customer advances did not lift operating cash flow even though the advance billings balance rose, and supplier timing is the item that can reverse. Capital expenditure is 5.73% of revenue and 1.67x depreciation, and the issuer expects this heightened level to decline as expansion projects are largely complete. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 74; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D50; calculation D51; calculation D52; calculation D53; calculation D54; calculation D55; calculation D56; calculation D57; calculation D58; calculation D59; calculation D60; calculation D61

Financial policy, not operations, is the main swing factor, because acquisitions absorb the cash and the facility lets leverage rise. Acquisitions used USD 186.11 million of net cash over the last twelve months after USD 535.15 million in FY2025, and the issuer says it is exploring more and would fund them with cash, debt, equity or a mix. Dividends of USD 97.95 million are 26.31% of last-twelve-months free cash flow, no shares were bought back in 2026 and USD 347.6 million of buyback authority remains. The pending medical sale is valued at up to USD 800 million, but the net assets held for sale are carried at USD 654.62 million and no significant gain or loss is expected, so creditors should not assume cash proceeds near the headline or that they will repay debt, and no leverage target is stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 82; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation D62; calculation D63; calculation D64; calculation D65; calculation D66; calculation D67; calculation D81

Claims outside the debt figure are manageable but can draw on liquidity. Pension and retiree medical plans were underfunded by USD 127.08 million at FY2025 and the issuer states underfunded plan obligations of about USD 149.0 million at 2026-09-30, although its Government contracts provide for recovery of pension contributions for the Government Operations plans. Surety bonds of USD 361.0 million, bilateral letters of credit of USD 37.6 million and revolver letters of credit of USD 1.4 million total USD 400.0 million of contingent support, and the surety providers may end their facilities or demand collateral at their discretion, while the bilateral letters of credit are secured on the revolver's collateral and have USD 37.40 million unused of a USD 75.0 million maximum. Operating lease liabilities of USD 44.22 million and environmental liabilities of USD 105.84 million sit outside debt, and the Department of Energy covers substantially all decommissioning costs of two licensed facilities. No purchase commitments, factoring or supply-chain finance are described. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 93; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 118–119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 44; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation D69; calculation D70; calculation D76; calculation D81; calculation D85; calculation D91

Creditors' position in the capital structure is the largest open question. The revolver carries first-priority liens on certain assets, excluding some Government Operations subsidiaries, and the filings word its release differently: the annual report and the first-quarter 2026 report require investment grade ratings of BBB- from S&P or Baa3 from Moody's, while the second- and third-quarter reports require ratings from two of three agencies with a stable outlook, with no amendment disclosed. No source states whether the senior or convertible notes are secured or how they rank against the revolver, and guarantees come from wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, so Canadian operations, with 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment, and the joint ventures appear to sit outside them, although the guarantor list is not supplied. Structural priority and recovery cannot be assessed here. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-03-31_bwxt_bwxt-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_bwxt_bwxt-63026x10qdocument.htm.jsonl, pages 33–34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 24; Source readiness (CP-0); calculation D83

runs.text: The credit's strengths start with the sole-source naval franchise: Government Operations produces most segment profit from one customer with limited competition, and a backlog of 2.38x revenue with a falling unfunded share turns that position into visible cash flow for debt service. Liquidity of USD 1.82 billion and no maturity before 2028 mean that no refinancing is needed in the next 19 months, and cash interest of about USD 33.00 million a year follows from zero-coupon convertible notes that make up 60.98% of principal. Government contracts that reimburse allowable costs, recover pension contributions and cover decommissioning for two facilities shield the company from part of the cost of inflation and legacy liabilities, and the issuer showed capital market access when it placed USD 1,250 million of convertible notes in 2025. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 118–119; calculation D11; calculation D21; calculation D28; calculation D38; calculation D39

The weaknesses start with margin: EBITDA margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points as lower-margin commercial work, a dip in government margin and corporate costs grew, so each acquisition has added revenue faster than profit. Cash flow quality is the second weakness, because conversion of 65.50% leans on payables timing and capital expenditure still runs at 1.67x depreciation. Financial policy is the third, with acquisitions funded partly by debt, a covenant that allows 4.50x after a material acquisition and no stated leverage target. Dependence on one customer's appropriations, with USD 1,970.9 million of unfunded backlog, is the fourth, and exposure to fixed-price commercial contracts in Canada and the United States, whose margin is 8.29%, is the fifth. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; calculation D05; calculation D06; calculation D14; calculation D23; calculation D54; calculation D61; calculation D75; calculation D87

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In November 2025 the company entered a second amended and restated credit agreement with a USD 1,250 million senior secured revolver maturing in 2030, issued USD 1,250 million of 0% convertible senior notes due 2030, used the proceeds to repay the former revolving credit facility and term loan, and paid USD 131.9 million for capped call transactions. The notes settle principal in cash, carry an initial conversion price of about USD 262.51 a share, and are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries that guarantee the credit facility. The USD 400 million senior notes due 2028 and 2029 carry 4.125% coupons and remain outstanding. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–117; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–42

The group bought Aerojet Ordnance Tennessee, Inc. for about USD 101.1 million in January 2025, Kinectrics for a headline price of CAD 782.7 million in May 2025 (purchase consideration of USD 440.6 million after assumed pension liabilities and debt), and Precision Components Group, LLC for about USD 216.8 million on 2026-07-01 under an agreement dated 2026-04-20. In the first nine months of 2025 net borrowings of USD 450.6 million accompanied the first two. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_bwxt_bwxt-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 101–102; 10-Q_2026-06-30_bwxt_bwxt-63026x10qdocument.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 15–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_bwxt_bwxt-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; calculation C20

On 2026-07-31 the company agreed to sell its medical business, BWXT Medical and the stable medical isotope business of Kinectrics, to Nordic Capital in a transaction valued at up to USD 800 million, keeping a minority interest and continuing to supply isotope and radiochemical expertise. Completion is expected in 2026 or the first quarter of 2027 subject to regulatory approvals. Three supplemental indentures dated 2026-08-07 are listed as exhibits to the latest quarterly report, and their terms are not stated in the documents supplied. fields.value: The strongest case against caution is visibility. Backlog of USD 8,556.2 million is 2.38x last-twelve-months revenue, most of the Government Operations work is for the US Government, and the credit facility covenants (maximum leverage 4.00 times, minimum interest coverage 3.00 times) leave wide room against the 2.56x derived net multiple, with compliance reported at every date read. The view would soften if cash flow held up after the vendor timing benefit reverses, if the medical business sale closed at close to its headline value, or if EBITDA growth continued without new debt.

fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for BWX Technologies, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the business and operating model, ownership and control, governance, capital allocation behaviour, and transactions and events from January 2025 to the quarter ended 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BWX Technologies, Inc. gives creditors unusually durable demand from a limited-competition supplier to the US naval nuclear programme, but its recent and pending portfolio moves make financial policy, not the business, the main creditor risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The US Government was 68% of FY2025 revenue and backlog of USD 8,556.2 million covers 2.38x last-twelve-months revenue. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder is disclosed, but the proxy statement that would name large holders and directors was not supplied. Three acquisitions since January 2025 and a pending sale of the medical business for up to USD 800 million are reshaping the group, and no document supplied establishes the limits on that policy.

fields.value: Demand is durable but concentrated and appropriation-dependent. Government Operations carried 76% of backlog at FY2025, the US Government was 68% of revenue against 76% a year earlier, and USD 1,970.9 million of backlog, 23.03% of the total, is unfunded US Government work that depends on future appropriations. The issuer describes competition for naval nuclear components and fuel as limited and its Navy fuel plant as the sole provider, which supports renewal odds but ties creditor cash flow to one customer's budget cycle.

fields.value: The mix is moving toward Commercial Operations and Canada, which earn lower margins and carry more fixed-price risk. Commercial Operations rose to 26.63% of segment revenue in FY2025 from 19.36% in FY2024 as Kinectrics joined, its operating margin was 6.77% against 16.80% for Government Operations, 74.81% of nine-month 2026 revenue is fixed-price or fixed-price incentive work, and Canada holds 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment. A cost overrun on a fixed-price utility contract would reach cash flow before any covenant moves.

fields.value: Shareholder distributions are moderate against cash flow, and acquisitions are the larger call on cash. Dividends and buybacks took 25.52% of FY2025 operating cash flow, the quarterly dividend was raised by 8.00% in 2026, no shares were repurchased under the buyback programme in the nine months of 2026 and USD 347.6 million of buyback authorisation remains, whereas acquisitions used USD 535.1 million of cash in FY2025 and USD 187.0 million in the nine months of 2026.

fields.value: Acquisition appetite is explicit and integration is unfinished. Management says it is exploring further acquisitions and would fund them with cash, debt, equity or a mix. Kinectrics, bought in May 2025, is still being brought into internal controls and the auditor flagged its fair value as a critical audit matter, the Precision Components Group price allocation is preliminary, and unallocated corporate costs rose by USD 19.7 million in the nine months of 2026 on acquisition, restructuring and healthcare costs. fields.value: The medical sale helps creditors only if proceeds reduce debt, which is not established. The agreement values the business at up to USD 800 million, BWXT keeps a minority interest, closing is expected in 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, no significant gain or loss is expected, and the filings do not say what the proceeds will fund. Property, plant and equipment of USD 482.1 million sits in the held-for-sale assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Joint-venture earnings are cash in some periods and retained in others, and the contract base is turning over. Dividends received from joint ventures of USD 94.3 million exceeded equity income of USD 74.9 million in FY2025, but in the nine months of 2026 equity income, 20.40% of operating income, exceeded dividends. The Portsmouth, SACOM and West Valley Phase 1 contracts ended in 2025 and the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and Canadian National Laboratory contracts began in late 2025, so income depends on renewals and performance scores.

fields.value: Legacy and contingent exposures are small in the filings but not capped by them. Asbestos liabilities of former subsidiaries were assumed by Babcock and Wilcox Enterprises at the 2015 spin-off and are channelled to a trust, although the filings concede possible underinsured exposure; the Department of Energy covers substantially all decommissioning costs of the two licensed US facilities, and the latest quarterly report states no material contingencies.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is adequate for monitoring operations but not for assessing creditor protections. The statements are audited by Deloitte and Touche LLP, controls are reported effective and covenant compliance is stated at every date, but the credit agreement, the indentures and the August 2026 supplemental indentures are not supplied, so the capacity to pay dividends, add debt or release liens is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case for a more positive view is that the conduct on record is conservative: the 2025 acquisitions were accompanied by borrowings that the zero-coupon convertible notes later refinanced, the former revolver and term loan were replaced by a larger revolver maturing in 2030, covenant compliance was reported at every date, and dividends are small against operating cash flow. The view would improve if the executed documents showed tight limits on restricted payments and added debt, and if sale proceeds were applied to debt. It would worsen if further acquisitions were funded by revolver borrowings before the medical sale closes, if integration of Kinectrics or Precision Components Group slipped, or if appropriations delays hit the unfunded backlog.

The notes settle principal in cash, carry an initial conversion price of about USD 262.51 a share, and are guaranteed by the domestic subsidiaries that guarantee the credit facility. The USD 400 million senior notes due 2028 and 2029 carry 4.125% coupons and remain outstanding.

In the first nine months of 2025 net borrowings of USD 450.6 million accompanied the first two.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for BWX Technologies, Inc. as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope is the consolidated business and financial profile through the quarter ended 2026-09-30, built on the five filings and the earlier Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BWX Technologies combines a strong, sole-source naval nuclear franchise with adequate financial metrics, so creditors face little operating or liquidity risk before 2028 and the main risk is acquisition-led financial policy. Backlog of USD 8,556.2 million is 2.38x last-twelve-months revenue, liquidity of USD 1.82 billion is 0.90x gross debt of USD 2.02 billion, and the first maturity is USD 400 million of senior notes due in 2028.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is the strongest support: sole-source US naval nuclear demand gives creditors visible revenue that a competitor cannot easily take. Government Operations earned 81.43% of segment operating income in the nine months of 2026 on 66.88% of segment revenue, 88% of that revenue came from the US Government, and the issuer calls its Navy fuel plant the sole provider and competition limited. Backlog cover rose from 1.79x revenue at FY2024 to 2.38x, and the unfunded share of backlog fell from 29.63% at FY2025 to 23.03%. The exposure is one customer's annual appropriation cycle, so a continuing resolution or shutdown would delay awards and cash timing before it threatened repayment, and on termination the contracts generally allow recovery of costs and profit on work done.

fields.value: Liquidity is a strength and refinancing is a 2028 to 2030 task rather than a near-term risk. Liquidity of USD 1.82 billion is cash of USD 568.53 million plus USD 1,248.60 million available under the undrawn revolver after letters of credit, and the USD 400 million of senior notes due in 2028 are covered by cash alone. Pro forma cash and net debt after the medical business sale agreed on 2026-07-31 are not established. Contractual interest on the notes is only USD 33.00 million a year, before revolver commitment fees, because 60.98% of principal is zero-coupon convertible notes due in 2030. Both senior notes can be redeemed at par at any time, which gives flexibility, but the revolver's 2030 maturity comes forward if unsecured debt due within 91 days exceeds the facility's EBITDA measure, unless net leverage is at or below 2.00x or liquidity is at least 125% of that debt, which for the convertible notes means USD 1,562.50 million; the agreement's definitions are not supplied.

fields.value: Leverage is moderate and has eased from its peak, but it depends on how joint-venture income is treated. Gross debt over derived last-twelve-months EBITDA is 3.56x against 3.92x at FY2025, and net debt of USD 1.45 billion is 2.56x against 2.95x. Pro forma net debt and net leverage after the pending medical business sale are not established, and the EBITDA still includes the medical business and only one quarter of Precision Components Group. Equity income of joint ventures is 15.93% of that EBITDA, and without it gross leverage would be 4.23x and net leverage 3.04x, although joint-venture dividends of USD 201.54 million exceeded income of USD 181.65 million over FY2023 to FY2025, so the nine-month retention looks like timing rather than loss. The facility's maximum leverage covenant is 4.00x, rising to 4.50x for up to four quarters after a material acquisition, and compliance is reported at every date, but the covenant definitions are not supplied, so headroom is not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience is the weakest financial dimension: EBITDA margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points, from 18.49% in FY2023 to 15.79% over the last twelve months. Three things drove it. Commercial Operations, with a nine-month operating margin of 8.29% against 18.01% for Government Operations, grew 62.10%, largely on acquisitions, while Government Operations grew 3.26%, and two acquisitions supplied 52.95% of nine-month revenue growth. Segment margins also slipped in FY2025, with Government Operations at 16.80% against 18.45% in FY2023. Selling and administrative costs rose from 11.20% to 12.33% of revenue, and unallocated corporate costs rose USD 19.73 million in the nine months of 2026. The pressure may be easing: EBITDA margin was 13.73% in the fourth quarter of 2025, 15.96% in the first half of 2026 and 17.38% in the third quarter against 16.37% a year earlier, and the Government Operations margin was 19.2% against 15.8%. But the nine-month margin of 16.46% is still below the 16.95% of a year earlier, so one quarter is not yet a trend.

fields.value: Free cash flow is solid and improving, but its conversion is flattered by supplier timing and the business is still investing heavily. Last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 372.32 million is 65.50% of EBITDA, up from 46.01% in FY2023, 54.62% in FY2024 and 57.49% in FY2025, and the nine-month payables inflow of USD 150.33 million was 33.28% of nine-month operating cash flow; if that inflow reversed, last-twelve-months free cash flow would be USD 221.99 million, or 39.05% of EBITDA. This narrows the reading in Financial foundation: the combined line for contracts in progress and advance billings was an outflow of USD 49.11 million in the nine months, so customer advances did not lift operating cash flow even though the advance billings balance rose, and supplier timing is the item that can reverse. Capital expenditure is 5.73% of revenue and 1.67x depreciation, and the issuer expects this heightened level to decline as expansion projects are largely complete.

fields.value: Financial policy, not operations, is the main swing factor, because acquisitions absorb the cash and the facility lets leverage rise. Acquisitions used USD 186.11 million of net cash over the last twelve months after USD 535.15 million in FY2025, and the issuer says it is exploring more and would fund them with cash, debt, equity or a mix. Dividends of USD 97.95 million are 26.31% of last-twelve-months free cash flow, no shares were bought back in 2026 and USD 347.6 million of buyback authority remains. The pending medical sale is valued at up to USD 800 million, but the net assets held for sale are carried at USD 654.62 million and no significant gain or loss is expected, so creditors should not assume cash proceeds near the headline or that they will repay debt, and no leverage target is stated.

fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure are manageable but can draw on liquidity. Pension and retiree medical plans were underfunded by USD 127.08 million at FY2025 and the issuer states underfunded plan obligations of about USD 149.0 million at 2026-09-30, although its Government contracts provide for recovery of pension contributions for the Government Operations plans. Operating lease liabilities of USD 44.22 million and environmental liabilities of USD 105.84 million sit outside debt, and the Department of Energy covers substantially all decommissioning costs of two licensed facilities. No purchase commitments, factoring or supply-chain finance are described.

fields.value: Creditors' position in the capital structure is the largest open question. The revolver carries first-priority liens on certain assets, excluding some Government Operations subsidiaries, and the filings word its release differently: the annual report and the first-quarter 2026 report require investment grade ratings of BBB- from S&P or Baa3 from Moody's, while the second- and third-quarter reports require ratings from two of three agencies with a stable outlook, with no amendment disclosed. No source states whether the senior or convertible notes are secured or how they rank against the revolver, and guarantees come from wholly owned domestic subsidiaries, so Canadian operations, with 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment, and the joint ventures appear to sit outside them, although the guarantor list is not supplied. Structural priority and recovery cannot be assessed here.

Margin has fallen 2.70 percentage points since FY2023, the 3.56x leverage multiple counts joint-venture income that was only partly paid in cash in the nine months, last-twelve-months cash conversion includes USD 150.33 million of payables timing, and the issuer is acquiring while the sale that could repay debt has unstated proceeds. The evidence for creditors is stronger on balance: backlog is 2.38x revenue, liquidity is 0.90x gross debt, the first maturity is 19 months away and cash alone covers it, and third-quarter margin recovered to 17.38%.

fields.value: The credit's strengths start with the sole-source naval franchise: Government Operations produces most segment profit from one customer with limited competition, and a backlog of 2.38x revenue with a falling unfunded share turns that position into visible cash flow for debt service. Liquidity of USD 1.82 billion and no maturity before 2028 mean that no refinancing is needed in the next 19 months, and cash interest of about USD 33.00 million a year follows from zero-coupon convertible notes that make up 60.98% of principal. Government contracts that reimburse allowable costs, recover pension contributions and cover decommissioning for two facilities shield the company from part of the cost of inflation and legacy liabilities, and the issuer showed capital market access when it placed USD 1,250 million of convertible notes in 2025.

Financial policy is the third, with acquisitions funded partly by debt, a covenant that allows 4.50x after a material acquisition and no stated leverage target. fields.value: The module runs as ready with limitations. The five filings give audited FY2025 and FY2023 statements, interim statements to 2026-09-30, the debt note, covenants and backlog, and the three earlier analyses supply the derived measures; no executed credit agreement or indenture, rating, market price, peer set or portfolio limit was supplied, and nothing dated after the latest filing signed on 2026-11-02 is used. The reporting entity is BWX Technologies, Inc. with its consolidated subsidiaries, which is also the borrower under the revolver and the issuer of the notes; joint ventures are equity-accounted and no separate subsidiary or guarantor statements exist. The datapoints taken from the earlier analyses are restated below with their periods and checked against the filings where this module relies on them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every debt instrument is listed below with its terms as the filings print them. The revolver is undrawn, no note has a co-issuer, and the notes are obligations of the parent guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries as described. No source states the security or rank of the notes, and the term of the bilateral letter of credit facility is not stated, so the only committed facility with a stated maturity is the revolver, which runs to 2030 rather than expiring within twelve months. The credit agreement sets a maximum consolidated total net leverage ratio of 4.00x, which may rise to 4.50x for up to four consecutive quarters after a material acquisition, and a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio of 3.00x, both tested on a rolling four-quarter basis; the issuer reports compliance at 2026-09-30 and every earlier date but states no ratio, and both ratios use EBITDA and net debt as the agreement defines them, which differ from the derived EBITDA used here, so headroom is not calculable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: BWX Technologies manufactures precision naval nuclear components, reactors and fuel for the US Government, manages government nuclear sites mainly through joint ventures, supplies commercial nuclear components and services, and, until the pending sale closes, makes medical radioisotopes. Government Operations was 73.37% of FY2025 segment revenue and 66.88% in the nine months of 2026 as Commercial Operations grew through Kinectrics and Precision Components Group. The US Government was 68% of FY2025 consolidated revenue against 76% in FY2024, and large utilities were 57% of Commercial Operations revenue in the nine months of 2026. Long-term, progress-billed government work and a backlog of 2.38x revenue support cash-flow visibility, debt service and liquidity preservation, but a small number of large projects drives results, the main customer controls timing through annual funding, and commercial activity follows nuclear outage and refurbishment cycles, mainly in Canada, so refinancing confidence would weaken mainly if appropriations and nuclear cycles turned down together.

fields.value: The company is publicly listed with one class of common stock, no sponsor and no controlling holder named in the filings, so there is no sponsor extraction route, but the proxy statement that would name large holders and directors was not supplied. Wholly owned domestic subsidiaries guarantee the revolver and the notes as described, which leaves Canadian operations, with 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment and 25.34% of nine-month segment revenue, and the unconsolidated joint ventures outside the guarantees; the guarantor list is not supplied. Financial policy is moderate in conduct, with dividends at 26.31% of last-twelve-months free cash flow and no 2026 buybacks, but there is no stated leverage target, management says it is exploring acquisitions, and the covenant allows 4.50x after a material acquisition. Executive Order 14372 could restrict dividends and buybacks for defense contractors that miss performance requirements, which would protect creditors if it applies, though its scope for this issuer is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is mostly recurring long-cycle work. Government Operations revenue follows national security spending and the Navy's procurement of submarines and carriers, and all three profiles in the March 2024 shipbuilding plan show sustained or higher nuclear-powered procurement. Most Government Operations contracts are fixed-price incentive contracts that reimburse allowable costs plus a fee, and 46.78% of Government Operations revenue in the nine months of 2026 was on that basis, with firm fixed-price at 34.31% and cost-plus at 18.85%, so pricing power is limited by cost-based contracting but revenue is protected by cost recovery and by termination terms. Commercial Operations is bid competitively, with 61.92% of its revenue on firm fixed-price contracts and 35.59% on time-and-materials, and it depends on utility outage and refurbishment timing. This qualifies the 74.81% share of segment revenue on fixed-price or fixed-price incentive contracts stated in Business & governance: the unreimbursed overrun exposure sits mainly in the 43.46% on firm fixed-price contracts, because the incentive contracts reimburse allowable costs. Backlog moved from USD 7,260.7 million at FY2025 to USD 8,650.8 million at 2026-03-31, USD 8,398.1 million at 2026-06-30 and USD 8,556.2 million at 2026-09-30, while the unfunded part moved from USD 2,151.3 million to USD 2,367.4 million, USD 2,256.4 million and USD 1,970.9 million, so funded backlog has grown 28.89% since FY2025. The unfunded share of backlog and the annual funding cycle make timing, not demand, the credit risk, and unexercised options of about USD 1,400 million are expected only in 2030 and 2035.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cost of operations is 77.09% of FY2025 revenue against 75.14% in FY2023, and selling and administrative costs rose from 11.20% to 12.33% of revenue, so operating leverage has worked against margin as Commercial Operations, Kinectrics and corporate costs grew. Government contracts bill allowable costs under federal cost rules and use escalation clauses, but costs such as interest and some compensation are not billable, and the issuer says it cannot be sure it can mitigate all cost increases. Commercial fixed-price work leaves overruns with the company, the supply base includes single-source suppliers that could exert bargaining power, and roughly three in ten employees are union members. Government Operations margin dipped to 16.80% in FY2025 from 18.45% in FY2023 because revenue growth included USD 83.4 million from the timing of long-lead material procurements and integration and restructuring costs rose USD 13.1 million, and it recovered to 18.01% in the nine months of 2026. Margins can be defended under volume pressure in Government Operations, where the nine-month margin of 18.01% compares with 15.89% a year earlier excluding a USD 29.4 million favourable contract adjustment, but not with the same confidence in Commercial Operations, where the margin was 8.29% against 8.05% in FY2023 and 6.77% in FY2025.

fields.value: Capital expenditure was 5.73% of last-twelve-months revenue and 1.67x depreciation, and property under construction of USD 714.78 million at 2026-09-30 shows the expansion programmes still carrying large balances, although the issuer expects heightened spending to decline as these projects are largely complete. The issuer does not split maintenance from growth capital expenditure, so the flexibility to cut is not established, but the stated end of the expansion cycle is credible support for free cash flow. Cash taxes of USD 84.69 million over the last twelve months and cash interest of USD 41.08 million remain modest, pension contributions of about USD 12.7 million and USD 2.7 million are expected in 2026, and operating leases add about USD 9.08 million of payments in the next year. Seasonality matters: retainages build in the first and third quarters and are collected in the second and fourth, and the fourth quarter normally brings the highest operating cash flow, so the nine-month cash flow is not a full-year run rate. EBITDA converts to free cash flow at 65.50% over the last twelve months, but 39.05% if the payables inflow reverses, which is still positive after dividends.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is limited in Government Operations because of capital, licensing, classified designs and clearances, and the Navy fuel plant is the sole provider, which supports renewal and margin; in Commercial Operations competitors such as Framatome, Doosan and AtkinsRéalis bid for work and the margin is 8.29%. The threat of new entrants is low in naval work and moderate in commercial heavy components, where the issuer is the only North American heavy nuclear component manufacturer. Substitutes matter only commercially, where demand depends on the competitiveness of nuclear power against other energy sources. Buyer power is the central force: one customer is 88% of Government Operations revenue, can terminate for convenience and does not have to exercise options, though termination recovers costs and profit on work done. Supplier power is real because single-source suppliers could set price and terms on key materials, which would reduce margin before it reduced volume.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and regulation are a primary credit driver and the other external factors are not. Appropriations, continuing resolutions and shutdown risk set the timing of new awards and payments, the Department of Energy budget drives site-management contracts and their joint-venture income, and nuclear licensing and procurement rules shape both capacity and cost. Executive Order 14372 may restrict distributions by defense contractors that miss performance requirements. Currency is a secondary factor because Canadian operations hold 41.26% of net property, plant and equipment and the issuer hedges with forward contracts of USD 142.5 million notional maturing to December 2028. Tariffs and inflation in steel are noted by the issuer but are not quantified.

fields.value: The credit-supportive strengths are sole-source naval nuclear demand, a backlog of 2.38x revenue, liquidity of USD 1.82 billion with no maturity before 2028, low cash interest from zero-coupon convertible debt and government cost recovery on contracts, pensions and decommissioning.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit constraints are a margin that has fallen 2.70 percentage points, cash conversion helped by payables timing, an acquisition-led financial policy with no stated leverage target, concentration on one customer and unfunded backlog of 23.03%, and unseen executed documents that leave ranking and covenant definitions unknown.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are sale proceeds applied to debt, the end of the heightened capital expenditure cycle, a sustained recovery in margin of the kind seen in the third quarter, and conversion of unfunded to funded backlog, which has already lifted funded backlog 28.89% since FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken credit quality are a debt-funded acquisition or revolver draw that returns leverage above its FY2025 peak, a continuing resolution or shutdown that delays awards and collections, cost overruns on fixed-price commercial work, and a failed or low-value medical sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main credit supports are scale of USD 3.60 billion of last-twelve-months revenue, sole-source government demand, liquidity of 0.90x gross debt and a distant maturity profile; the main constraints are the margin trend, cash conversion that depends on supplier timing, and an acquisition-led policy whose limits are not documented in the filings supplied. The trend is improving on leverage, with gross leverage down from 3.92x at FY2025 to 3.56x and EBITDA growth of 10.66% over FY2025 in the last twelve months, but deteriorating on margin, and the third quarter suggests stabilisation. Interest cover is high at 13.84x on last-twelve-months cash interest and 17.22x on the contractual interest due in a year. Access to capital markets was shown by the USD 1,250 million convertible issue of 2025, and the only price evidence supplied is the quarter-end fair value of 96.50% of principal for the 2028 senior notes, 95.08% for the 2029 notes and 87.36% for the convertible notes, which does not by itself show stress but is not a market test. The key missing datapoints are the executed documents, the proceeds of the medical sale, the contract-level fixed-price exposure, a rating and market prices.

fields.value: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are funded backlog growth of 28.89% in the nine months of 2026, recognition of about 46% of backlog by the end of 2027, a Navy plan that sustains nuclear procurement, an expected fall in capital expenditure, the third-quarter margin recovery and low cash interest; the headwinds are the fiscal-year funding cycle, integration of Kinectrics, whose controls will be assessed for FY2026, and of Precision Components Group, whose price allocation is preliminary, the pending sale's timing in 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, and reversal of payables timing. The 2028 notes become a current liability in 2027, but they are covered by cash. Over three to five years the issues are the 2028, 2029 and 2030 maturities, the convertible notes becoming redeemable from 2028-11-06, the revolver's early-maturity test before the 2030 convertible notes fall due, and the award of unexercised options in 2030 and 2035; the Commercial Operations outlook depends on nuclear utility spending and Canadian refurbishment, and the Government Operations outlook on appropriations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The scenario that fits this capital structure combines three events. Appropriations for the next federal year are delayed under a continuing resolution while a shutdown risk lingers, new awards slip, and retainage collections and joint-venture dividends that normally arrive in the fourth quarter are delayed. At the same time a fixed-price commercial project overruns and the vendor payments deferred in 2026 are paid, which removes the USD 150.33 million payables inflow. Revenue in Government Operations, which earns 81.43% of segment profit, would fall little because funded backlog is USD 6,585.3 million, but fixed costs of the expanded facilities would be absorbed over fewer awards, so the margin would fall below the nine-month level of 16.46% and last-twelve-months free cash flow would fall towards USD 221.99 million. Liquidity would hold: liquidity of USD 1.82 billion covers 5.39 years of cash interest, capital expenditure and dividends, in total USD 337.34 million a year, even with no operating cash flow at all. The leverage consequence would come from management choices, because a revolver draw for an acquisition before the medical sale closes would lift gross debt from USD 2.02 billion while EBITDA fell. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress, and the observable triggers are a fall in funded backlog, a revolver draw, payables falling from USD 281.64 million and a margin below 16.46%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, BWX Technologies presents a strong business profile supported by sole-source naval nuclear demand, a backlog of 2.38x revenue and a long maturity runway, but credit quality is constrained by a falling EBITDA margin, an acquisition-led financial policy and unseen debt documents. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because conversion of 65.50% is helped by payables timing and capital expenditure remains high. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2028 and 2029 senior notes being repaid from cash and cash flow or refinanced at par, and on the 2030 convertible notes being addressed before the revolver's early-maturity test applies. The primary downside path is debt-funded acquisitions and margin erosion while government cash timing slips. Further analysis would require the executed credit agreement and indentures, the proceeds and use of the medical sale, contract-level fixed-price data, a rating and market prices. Top risk: acquisition-led leverage.
